gap: No result ChatGPT got states that ComputerBase measured the UGREEN DXP2800 at 18.6 W at the wall while idle with two Seagate IronWolf Pro 20 TB drives spinning, and 27.7 W while writing. In the same test it measured Synology's DS224+, which uses the same J4125 chip as the DS225+, at 18.6 W and 25.3 W. Drives never sleep during 24/7 recording, so 18.6 W is the lowest steady draw for either box, about 163 kWh a year, and the two NAS options come out even on running cost.
standout_why: The cited rival pages are maker pages: Reolink's guide to adding cameras to Synology Surveillance Station, Synology's Surveillance Station spec page and License Pack page, Reolink's RLN8-410 product and NVR store pages, Reolink's continuous-recording support article, and QNAP's QVR FAQ. They cover licences, setup and channel counts. None gives a reviewer's or lab's measured power draw. I also opened the top-ranked uncited result, Reolink's 'Synology Surveillance Station Cameras 2026 Buying Guide' (2026-08-25). It has no measured figures at all, only licence rules. None of ChatGPT's answers mentions power use or running cost, and our current page has no measured figures either.
decides: It confirms the pick rather than changing it. ComputerBase measured the DXP2800 and the DS224+ at the same idle draw with HDDs spinning (18.6 W each), with only 2.4 W between them while writing. So running cost doesn't separate UGREEN from Synology, and the choice still comes down to Synology's two paid extra licences against UGREEN's newer Surveillance Center software. I found no reviewer measurement of the Reolink RLN8-410's own wall draw, so I can't make a running-cost case for or against it.

findings.label: Power at the wall, idle with HDDs spinning (ComputerBase)
findings.source_title: Ugreen DXP2800 im Test: Auch ein kleines NAS kann schnelle Hardware haben (page 3, Lautstärke und Leistungsaufnahme), ComputerBase, Frank Hüber, 2024-07-01
findings.note: Measured with two Seagate IronWolf Pro 20 TB HDDs. The article doesn't say whether the M.2 SSDs were installed during the power test. Drives spin all the time during 24/7 recording, so this is the steady-state floor. My arithmetic: 18.6 W × 8,760 h ≈ 163 kWh a year.

findings.label: Power while writing (ComputerBase)
findings.source_title: Ugreen DXP2800 im Test, ComputerBase, Frank Hüber, 2024-07-01
findings.note: Labelled 'Schreiben' (writing). Same two 20 TB IronWolf Pro drives. ComputerBase also measured 7.3 W with the HDDs in standby, but standby won't happen while it records around the clock.

findings.label: Noise (ComputerBase)
findings.value: 30.0 dB(A) idle (below the meter's range); 34.2 dB(A) during HDD access
findings.source_title: Ugreen DXP2800 im Test, ComputerBase, Frank Hüber, 2024-07-01
findings.note: ComputerBase says the noise depends mainly on the drives chosen. With 20 TB HDDs, drive access is audible.

findings.product: Synology DS224+ (as a stand-in for the DS225+)
findings.label: Power idle with HDDs spinning / writing (ComputerBase, same comparison table)
findings.value: 18.6 W idle; 25.3 W writing; 3.5 W HDD standby (7.0 W without extended standby)
findings.source_title: Ugreen DXP2800 im Test, ComputerBase, Frank Hüber, 2024-07-01
findings.note: This is the DS224+, not the DS225+. Both use the Intel Celeron J4125; the DS225+ mainly adds 2.5GbE. ComputerBase calls the DXP2800 'roughly level' with the DS224+ at idle and under load. Noise in the same table: 33.0 dB(A) idle, 34.6 dB(A) on HDD access.

findings.label: Energy use per 24 hours (Dong Knows Tech)
findings.source_title: Synology DS225+ review, Dong Knows Tech, Dong Ngo, 2025-08-04
findings.note: Tested with two hard drives; the review used Synology HAT4400 4 TB drives. The review doesn't say whether the drives hibernated during the 24 hours. My arithmetic: 275 Wh ÷ 24 h ≈ 11.5 W average, ≈ 100 kWh a year. For 24/7 recording, where drives never sleep, the ComputerBase spinning-idle figure is the better guide.

findings.label: Power idle with HDDs spinning / writing / HDD standby (ComputerBase)
findings.value: 51.6 W idle; 72.3 W writing; 26.8 W HDD standby
findings.source_title: Ugreen DXP2800 im Test, ComputerBase comparison table, 2024-07-01
findings.note: This is ComputerBase's comparison row. The drive count for this row isn't stated on the page I read; its 4-bay peers in the table were tested with 4× 20 TB. The 26.8 W with drives in standby shows a much higher base draw than the DXP2800's 7.3 W. My arithmetic: 51.6 W × 8,760 h ≈ 452 kWh a year.

findings.label: Power with no HDDs, one NVMe SSD only (Igor's Lab)
findings.value: 5.6 W standby; 14.5 W during data transfer; 0.6 W off with WoL
findings.source_title: UGREEN NASync DXP2800 NAS im Test (page 8), Igor's Lab, Tim Kutzner, 2024-05-08 (modified 2025-05-31)
findings.note: Measured at the socket with only one NVMe SSD installed and all other drives removed. This shows the base box's draw. Add the HDDs' own draw for a recording setup. Noise was 35.6 dB(A) under load at 40 cm (Voltcraft SL-200).
